title: Stale-telemetry oscillation
summary: Herding is a smooth function of staleness, and it is steep: a twelvefold goodput collapse across scrape intervals that all look reasonable.

steps.title: Least-requests, telemetry fresh
body: Least-requests routing, 100 ms telemetry publication interval: 14,912 tok/s goodput, 79.3% attainment, load spread 0.67.
This is not yet the correct-signal case from finding 1 — least-requests is still weaker than sampling — but at this interval the fleet has barely started to ring.
steps.look_for: A heatmap with visible but not extreme imbalance, matching a load spread of 0.67.

steps.title: 250 ms: almost nothing happens
body: Goodput 14,941 tok/s, attainment 79.5%, load spread 0.71 — essentially unchanged from 100 ms.
Between 100 and 250 ms almost nothing happens. Staleness has a threshold rather than a gradient, set by how fast queues change: the loop's own time constant.
steps.look_for: The heatmap looking almost identical to the previous step, not a smooth drift.

steps.title: 1 second: past the threshold
body: At 500 ms goodput was already down to 11,771 tok/s (64.8% attainment, spread 0.95). At 1 second it is 6,943 tok/s, 39.4% attainment, spread 1.27.
Nothing about the fleet changed; only how old the information was when the routing decision was made.
steps.look_for: The goodput line dropping sharply relative to throughput, which barely moves.

steps.title: 4 seconds: a twelvefold collapse from where we started
body: 2 seconds gives 3,494 tok/s (22.6% attainment, spread 1.54). 4 seconds gives 1,264 tok/s, 10.6% attainment, spread 1.88 — a twelvefold goodput collapse across a range of intervals that all look reasonable on a dashboard.
Every router agrees about which replica looked idle four seconds ago, and every router sends work to it. By the time the snapshot updates, that replica is the most loaded one in the fleet.
steps.look_for: A travelling wave rather than a static hot row: the pattern moves because the herd moves, not because the work does.

steps.title: The fix is not a better metric, it is a different sampling shape
body: Open the A/B view with A = the 4 s interval and B = the 100 ms interval to see the same seed and arrivals, only staleness differing.
Finding 1's lesson still holds underneath this one: power-of-two-choices tolerates staleness that least-requests cannot, because only a fraction of routers consider any one replica at once.
steps.look_for: Attainment moving from 10.6% to 79.3% with nothing changed but the scrape interval.
